description: Figure 5 presents a horizontal stacked bar chart showing the distribution (in percent) of “deceived conversations” across different degrees of ambiguity, with 4 categories (Academic Collaboration, Recruitment, Academic Funding, and Journalism) plotted as separate horizontal bars. Each bar is divided into 3 colored slices corresponding to ambiguity levels indicated by a legend on the right: “Yes” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “No” (green). Visually, Academic Collaboration appears split into a large red segment (roughly around half), a substantial yellow segment (around two-fifths), and a small green segment (around one-tenth); Recruitment shows a red segment a bit over half, a yellow segment around one-third, and a green segment around one-tenth; Academic Funding is dominated by a red segment (roughly around nine-tenths) with a small yellow segment (around one-tenth) and little to no visible green; Journalism shows a large yellow segment (roughly around three-quarters), a smaller red segment (around one-fifth), and a small green segment (around one-tenth). The x-axis is labeled “Number of Conversations” with tick marks (approximately 0 to 60), there are no percentage labels printed inside the slices, and no segments are exploded or otherwise emphasized beyond the color coding.
